title: Reconcile lint, types, tests and package boundaries

producerBaseline.scope: All four producer partitions, from the single final checkpoint run recorded in final-checkpoint/. Totals are the test frameworks' own, read from Bun's JUnit and Vitest's JSON reports and validated against what the wrapper dispatched -- not parsed from terminal output.
producerBaseline.nativeReports: The runners' own reports are committed alongside the logs: four lane records (<lane>.report.json) and 54 native framework reports (Bun JUnit XML, Vitest JSON) under the per-run <runId>-reports/ directories. The totals above are derived from these, not from terminal output.

findings.summary: New code violated the inherited ffprobe argv contract.
findings.detail: packages/studio-server/src/project/projectBatch.ts is new in this repository and built its ffprobe argv with no option terminator before the input path, so a media file whose name begins with a dash would be parsed as an option.
findings.consequence: The assertion was preserved and the caller fixed.

findings.summary: Concat positioned chunks by rounded container duration, corrupting frame rate.
findings.detail: The concat list had no duration directives, so the demuxer used each container's rounded duration: a 5-frame 30fps chunk reports 0.167000 rather than 0.166667, starting chunk 2 five ticks late at time base 1/15360 and making ffmpeg derive 30000/1001. At 24000/1001 it degraded to 287/12. Measured on our own ffmpeg 5.1.9, an -r-only variant still failed, proving the existing flag was a known-needed but insufficient mitigation.
findings.consequence: Durations are now derived from validated chunk frame ranges and the plan's rational rate. No re-encode, no new flags; timestamps corrected rather than the metadata label.
findings.creditedTo: external review supplied the rounding hypothesis and a runnable diagnostic

findings.summary: Peak correction cut broadband gain, destroying integrated loudness.
findings.detail: The correction lowered the entire signal to constrain a few peaks, so loudness fell by the full attenuation (5.9 LU). It also could not converge: each pass added the whole remaining deficit assuming linear response, but AAC overshoot is level-dependent. Attenuating 2.4 dB moved the measured peak UP from +1.4 to +2.3 dBFS, and the next pass compounded to -5.7 dB. Reproduces on ffmpeg 5.1.9 (5.9) and 7.1.5 (6.1), so it is not build variation.
findings.consequence: Replaced with a look-ahead limiter that reduces only what exceeds the ceiling, with level normalisation disabled. The loop lowers a limiter ceiling instead of accumulating gain, with a 0.5 dB overshoot margin, re-encoding from the original input so limiting is never stacked. Both the peak and loudness assertions pass; neither was weakened.
findings.creditedTo: external review corrected the diagnosis from true-peak to loudness and supplied stage measurements

findings.summary: The baseline claimed no files were left unlaunched while a committed log said 7 were.
findings.detail: The fail-fast integration/bun run printed that 7 selected files were not launched. I counted run summaries with a regex instead of reading the runner's verdict, trusting a derived count over the tool's own statement. Reporting unlaunched files is exactly the capability merged in PR #1.
findings.consequence: Corrected in BASELINE.md; the 7 files were run independently and now launch normally because the fail-fast cause is fixed. The runner was never modified to make a report look complete.

findings.classification: confirmed regression introduced by our own fix
findings.summary: The limiter fix delayed audio and truncated its tail.
findings.detail: Replacing the broadband gain cut with alimiter resolved the loudness defect but enabled no latency compensation. The limiter's look-ahead buffer shifts the signal and drops buffered tail samples. Reproduced on our own ffmpeg 5.1.9 with a 1kHz burst at a known offset: source first loud sample 24001, filtered 24240 - a 239-sample delay at 48kHz. This landed in audioPadTrim, whose entire purpose is making audio duration sample-exact against frameCount / fps.
findings.consequence: latency=1 added. Verified by deliberately removing the flag again: exactly the six new timing tests fail and the two original tests still pass, which demonstrates both that the new tests detect the regression and that the peak and loudness assertions never covered timing. An output can carry the correct duration, pass its peak ceiling and pass its loudness check while its content is delayed and its tail is truncated.
findings.creditedTo: external review found the regression and supplied the fix and tests as PR #2

findings.detail: audioLimiterTiming.fixture.ts used assert.ok(filter?.startsWith(...)), which does not narrow 'string | undefined' for TypeScript. tsc --noEmit failed with TS2322 where the value is passed to ffmpeg.
findings.consequence: Replaced with an explicit throw that narrows. Typecheck clean; the 8 tests still pass. The PR had listed typechecking as pending rather than claiming it.

findings.summary: Two follow-up regressions, both caught by existing contracts.
findings.detail: First, a unit test pinned the exact correction filter string, which PR #2 changed by adding the latency flag. Second, the ffprobe argv contract flagged the new timing fixture. The obvious fix there would have been wrong: the fixture spawns ffmpeg only and never ffprobe. The contract discovers callers by argv shape, deliberately over-including so a dependency-injected runner cannot hide, and an argv literal ending in a spread reads to it as a positional input requiring a terminator. That terminator is an ffprobe idiom - ffmpeg takes inputs via -i and its trailing positional is the output.
findings.consequence: The stale expectation was updated to the new filter. The fixture builds its argv by push rather than as a spread inside a literal, which states the shape accurately without weakening the contract or adding a meaningless terminator to ffmpeg calls.

findings.classification: false success in our own evidence tooling
findings.summary: The checkpoint generator reported passes it had never observed.
findings.detail: evidence/tickets/AFM-012/final-checkpoint/generate-receipt.mjs hard-coded exitCode: 0 for the acceptance suite, decided pass/fail by scanning console prose so an empty log read as a pass, and two of its detector patterns contained literal backspace bytes where word boundaries were intended, so 'FAIL:' was never matched at all. A tool built to stop hand-entered numbers had a success value typed into it.
findings.consequence: Replaced by tools/evidence/checkpoint-summary.mjs, whose rule is that a check passes only if it recorded an exit code and that exit code is 0. Absent evidence is 'unknown', never 'pass'. Run against the old evidence directory it returned NOT TRUSTWORTHY with 14 checks flagged 'no exit code recorded' — the same checks the old generator had called passing. 18 adversarial tests.

findings.summary: Every lane invocation recorded execution as permanently unknown.
findings.detail: lane-report.mjs modelled dispatch and execution as distinct correctly, but run-test-lane.mjs passed evidenceState: EVIDENCE.missing and frameworkResults: null for every invocation. No real run could ever produce framework-confirmed totals, so the distinction the module existed to preserve had no data behind it.
findings.consequence: framework-report.mjs binds a per-invocation report path before spawn, appends --reporter=junit/--reporter-outfile (bun) or --reporter=json/--outputFile (vitest), then reads the report back and validates it against the invocation. Both runners now report validated totals from real runs. Two parser defects were found only by spawning the real runners: Bun nests a testsuite element per describe block, and Vitest's numTotalTestSuites counts describes, so both overcounted collected files — which also trips the dispatch cross-check and would have rejected healthy evidence.
findings.creditedTo: external review identified this as the largest missing implementation step

findings.classification: checker too weak to establish its own claim
findings.summary: The boundary checker could be crossed seven ways without tripping.
findings.detail: Import extraction was regex-based over raw source and only direct imports inside the protected package were examined. A configured tsconfig paths alias, a chain through another first-party package, a test-scope helper that production code imports, a template-literal dynamic import, a .cts or .mts file, a direct puppeteer dependency, and a bare or subpath workspace import followed by convention to src/index rather than to the module the exports map actually serves — each reached forbidden code while the checker reported clean. It also reported a false positive on import-shaped text inside an ordinary string.
findings.consequence: Comments and string literals are stripped before scanning with line numbers preserved; aliases are read from tsconfig; first-party dependency paths are followed transitively and the full path reported, not just the endpoint; workspace imports resolve through the manifest's exports map with source conditions preferred over dist; browser-capture packages are named in every rule; and an import inside protected production code that cannot be resolved is reported rather than passed over, because silence would certify a boundary that was never checked. 33 tests, including the seven crossings and the false positive.
findings.creditedTo: external review supplied the crossings and the false positive

findings.classification: confirmed defect, concealed by the previous two
findings.summary: bun run lint had never completed; four real defects were hiding behind it.
findings.detail: Recording an exit code for every check showed the lint chain failing at its first link: check:docs-snippet-motion crashed with ENOENT because it pointed at docs/snippets/, the upstream repository's layout, while the import placed those files at docs/upstream/hyperframes/snippets/ under their retain-reference-docs disposition. The chain is &&-joined, so the ten checks after it never ran. Reporting oxlint's result alone had made the repository look clean.
findings.consequence: Four defects fixed. (1) packages/gcp-cloud-run/Dockerfile was missing project-model, diagram-viewer, diagram-engine and diagram-motion — manifests, sources and builds — so a Cloud Run image could not have built; the merge added them as producer dependencies and the Dockerfile was never updated. (2) diagram-engine and diagram-viewer declared no typecheck; the engine now typechecks its contracts.d.ts with skipLibCheck off, since that declaration file is the public type surface diagram-motion and project-model compile against, and the viewer carries a documented opt-out because it has no TypeScript at all. (3) A runtime dependency cycle core -> studio-server -> diagram-motion -> core. The checker carried an exception for the two-package core/studio-server component, to be deleted 'with the forwarding surface in the next breaking release'; the merge grew the component to three and it failed correctly. The exception was removed rather than widened: this repository has no published consumers, and every shim under core/src/studio-api/ re-exported code already living in studio-server, including three test files duplicated verbatim from studio-server's own. Seven import sites were repointed. (4) The skill mirror could not exist because /.claude/ was gitignored whole; the rule is now /.claude/* with the skills directory re-included, since it is tracked content rather than scratch and each CLI reads only its own path. scripts/publish-workflow.test.mjs was removed: it asserted on .github/workflows/publish.yml, which does not exist here because every upstream workflow was imported under quarantine-automation, a quarantine audit:automation already asserts.
findings.creditedTo: surfaced by the exit-code recording required by this ticket

findings.classification: enforcement and evidence checks too weak to support their own verdict
findings.summary: Three mechanisms accepted evidence that did not establish what it claimed.
findings.detail: External review executed the committed modules against disposable fixtures and produced six passing controls and ten failed rejections. Boundary enforcement: a specifier written './capture.js' whose source is 'capture.ts', a paths alias in a protected package's own tsconfig, real code inside a template interpolation, and a package whose root conditional exports overrides its main were all certified clean. Framework reporting: a JUnit document truncated mid-element still declared tests=8 and was read as eight passing cases; a Vitest report covering one of two dispatched files, or naming a file never dispatched at all, was accepted because the totals added up. Checkpoint completeness: a partition log with no EXIT marker was correctly called unknown and the overall checkpoint still printed PASS; deleting lint.log entirely passed, because root checks were discovered by listing logs rather than required by name; and a lane record claiming evidenceComplete with no execution counts passed with unknown totals.
findings.consequence: The scanner was replaced rather than patched again: syntax now comes from ts.createSourceFile and resolution from ts.resolveModuleName under the compiler options governing each file, so extension substitution, the nearest tsconfig's paths, and exports precedence are the compiler's behaviour rather than reimplementations of it. Report file identities survive parsing and are compared as sets, with a new EVIDENCE.incomplete state that keeps a partial run's real results without certifying the whole selection, and JUnit is checked for tag balance and for declared totals matching the cases present. The checkpoint declares REQUIRED_CHECKS in advance so an absent log is a reported absence, promotes an unknown partition verdict to a global problem, and validates the counts behind a completeness claim. All sixteen review cases pass, and every one is pinned in the repository's own suites. One behaviour changed as a consequence: a relative import to a file that does not exist is now reported unresolved, where textual path arithmetic had silently attributed it to a package.
findings.creditedTo: external review supplied the sixteen cases and a runnable reproducer

knownCoverageGaps: Windows frame staging is unverified: one case in windowsFrameStaging.test.ts is explicitly skipped on Linux. Recorded in skippedTests so the receipt agrees with the log rather than implying full coverage.

macOS system-font capture is unverified: two cases in deterministicFonts-systemCapture print a skip message, return early, and Bun records them as passing. They count among the passing cases but demonstrate nothing about macOS behaviour.
The limiter is a dynamics processor and changes audio character, not only level. Both assertions hold, but no test here evaluates perceptual quality; a human listen is warranted before shipping.

Byte-identical source establishes that those files were not edited, not that every effect of the fork is excluded. Dependencies, helpers, export resolution, configuration and native tool builds can still differ.
remainingAcceptance: Passing the inherited producer suites is not proof that the producer is correct.

Acceptance re-verifies the whole 7,786-file import on every run (SHA-256 over the tree for AFM-001, full-tree walks for AFM-003/005/006), which is ~10 of the ~15 minute checkpoint over a Windows bind mount. Splitting it into an import-integrity lane gated on _sources/ and provenance/import-map.json is not done.
packages/diagram-viewer's test script is `echo "no tests yet (AFM-030)" && exit 0`. It exits 0 and demonstrates nothing; AFM-030 owns it.

skippedTests.reason: Windows-specific frame staging; skipped on the Linux container. Platform coverage limitation, not a passing case.

finalCheckpoint.rule: A check passes only if it recorded an exit code and that exit code is 0. Absent evidence is 'unknown', never 'pass'. Console text may add detail; it may never establish success.
finalCheckpoint.scope: Sixteen checks executed in the pinned container against the source tree named by testedSourceTree. `lint` passing includes the Cloud Run Dockerfile workspace COVERAGE check; no Cloud Run image was built or deployed and none is claimed.

evidenceIntegrity: The checkpoint ran against the working tree, and that tree was fingerprinted before and after execution and found identical. Commit ee23fca2065e249ec05b96797942ea405748e093 carries exactly that tree, so testedSourceTree equals its tree object and `git cat-file -p ee23fca2065e249ec05b96797942ea405748e093` can be checked against it. This file was written afterward from that checkpoint's summary.json and is the only path differing between the tested tree and the commit that adds it; no source byte was changed after execution.

compatibilityBreaks.change: Removed @hyperframes/core/studio-api and its five subpath exports, along with the core -> studio-server dependency.
compatibilityBreaks.reason: Those files were deprecated forwarding shims re-exporting code that already lives in studio-server, and with diagram-motion added by the merge they completed a runtime cycle core -> studio-server -> diagram-motion -> core. The cycle checker's exception was written to be deleted 'with the forwarding surface in the next breaking release'.
compatibilityBreaks.effect: Consumers must import @hyperframes/studio-server directly. Seven in-repository import sites were repointed. This is an intentional breaking change in this fork, not an incidental cleanup.
